source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 3--4, especially Section 4.1 discussion of Theorem 4 and Section 4.2 discussion of Theorem 5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops design-based IPW/AIPW theory for general adaptive designs with fixed potential outcomes; Theorem 4 is its AIPW central-limit result and Theorem 5 supplies large-sample Wald-type confidence sets.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and main-text description of the adaptively weighted augmented-IPW estimator
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article constructs adaptive weighting for augmented-IPW policy evaluation and asymptotically normal confidence intervals; it does not formulate unrestricted uniformly honest expected-length minimaxity.

The paper gives design-based confidence intervals and confidence sequences for finite-population multi-arm bandits with arbitrary non-iid potential outcomes, rather than an all-kernel minimax confidence-length criterion.

The paper proves an efficient adaptive-AIPW CLT and develops fixed-time and time-uniform confidence procedures for sequential ATE experiments; it does not optimize expected length over all honest kernels.

The manuscript concerns inference conditional on realized stopping, assignment probabilities, and target parameter in batched bandits, with optimality under location-invariance or polyhedral restrictions.

The article develops selective randomization inference for adaptive experiments through conditioning on design-selection information and computes selective p-values/intervals; it does not prove a product prior posterior theorem for minimax confidence length.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2404.19118; corroborated by the 2025 Statistics in Medicine article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work studies identification and efficiency of concurrent versus nonconcurrent controls in platform trials, recommending concurrent cATE analysis under deterministic availability; it does not solve unrestricted confidence-length experiment comparison.

The paper studies minimax-optimal finite-population point-estimation designs and estimators for binary outcomes, with a second-order MSE expansion; it does not study honest interval length or outcome-adaptive allocation.
